definition: HTK (Hidden Markov Model Toolkit) is a proprietary software toolkit for handling HMMs.
details: It is mainly intended for speech recognition, but has been used in many other pattern recognition applications that employ HMMs, including speech synthesis, character recognition and DNA sequencing. Originally developed at the Machine Intelligence Laboratory (formerly known as the Speech Vision and Robotics Group) of the Cambridge University Engineering Department (CUED), the rights to sell HTK were acquired by Entropic Research Laboratory Inc. in 1993, and development was transferred to Entropic in 1995. Entropic was acquired by Microsoft in 1999, which subsequently licensed HTK back to CUED, allowing the university to resume distribution and development. HTK is now being widely used among researchers who are working on HMMs.

explainer.lead: HTK (Hidden Markov Model Toolkit) is a proprietary software toolkit for handling HMMs. It matters mainly for speech recognition but has been used in other HMM-based pattern recognition, including speech synthesis, character recognition, and DNA sequencing.

tiers.eli5: It is a toolbox for a statistical model that guesses sequences, most famously turning sound into words.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to build and train HMM-based recognizers, originally from Cambridge University's Machine Intelligence Laboratory, with selling rights acquired by Entropic Research Laboratory in 1993 and development transferred there. A pitfall is that it is proprietary software.
tiers.paperLevel: It is a software toolkit for handling Hidden Markov Models, chiefly for speech recognition and also for speech synthesis, character recognition, and DNA sequencing; it is a tool rather than a single formula.

explainer.example: A team trains an HMM acoustic model with HTK to recognize spoken words from audio.
